text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003ETwo vertebral arteries joins to form basilar artery.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E3.Patient is from a fluorosis\u0026nbsp; endemic area .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EEndemic fluorosis refers to that individuals living in a region characterized by high levels of fluorine in the drinking water; food and\/or air are thereby exposed to excessive amounts of this ion that resulted in general chronic accumulated fluorosis among many of them.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: arial;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/3295994\/\" style=\"background: transparent; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/3295994\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E4.How fluorosis mimics cervical spondylosis :\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003ESkeletal fluorosis can mimic various arthritis such as rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis or spondyloarthropathy.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003EThe early stages of the disease may be asymptomatic or present as vague pain in the neck or back with rigidity, arthralgia and paraesthesia in the limbs,\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003Eachilles tendinitis, and early morning stiffness\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: arial;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC9450208\/\" style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC9450208\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: arial;\"\u003E5.Cervical spondylosis is a progressive degenerative changes that affect all the components of cervical spine ( intervetebral discs,\u0026nbsp; joints..) in\u0026nbsp; general term for age-related wear and tear affecting the spinal disks in your neck. As the disks dehydrate and shrink, signs of osteoarthritis develop, including bony projections along the edges of bones (bone spurs).\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased !important; background-color: white; box-sizing: border-box; font-feature-settings: \u0026quot;kern\u0026quot;; font-kerning: normal; line-height: var(--mc-typography-line-height-6x); margin-block-end: var(--mc-spacing-2-5x); margin: 0px 0px 24px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003ECervical spondylosis is very common and worsens with age. More than 85% of people older than age 60 are affected by cervical spondylosis.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: arial;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/31855384\/\" style=\"background: transparent; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/31855384\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E6.How cervical spondylosis causing vertebrobasilar insufficiency :\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #333333; font-family: arial;\"\u003EVertebrobasilar insufficiency usually occurs in the presence of atherosclerosis or cervical spondylosis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #333333; font-family: arial;\"\u003Ebut symptoms can also arise when there is intermittent vertebral artery occlusion induced by extreme rotation or extension of the head. This mechanical compression of the vertebral arteries can occur along with other anomalies, including cervical osteophytes, fibrous bands, and osseous prominences.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: arial;\"\u003E\u003Ca She was asked to take Vertin 24 (betahistine) at discharge. she took the medication for 3 months and then stopped after consulting with her physician. She had mild episodes of vomiting for the next months until 3 days back when she had 5 episodes (severe)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/h3\u003E\u003Ch3 style=\"font-size: medium; font-weight: 400; text-align: left;\"\u003EVomiting-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/h3\u003E\u003Ch3 style=\"font-size: medium; font-weight: 400; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; non projectile, contents were food\/watery. there was no blood present in the vomitus. no temporal association with meal timings was noticed. it was associated with giddiness and colicky, non radiating pain in the epigastrium, present only during the episode. Not associated with fever, diarrhea or constipation.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/h3\u003E\u003Ch3 style=\"font-size: medium; font-weight: 400; text-align: left;\"\u003EFrequency of stools are normal but volume is decreased due to less food intake out of fear of vomiting.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/h3\u003E\u003Ch3 style=\"font-size: medium; font-weight: 400; text-align: left;\"\u003ENo history of-
